clue.text: Students with it are learning

definitions.meaning: students who hold a grant to fund their study are said to be on one
learning in the sense of deep academic knowledge

explanation.surface: A remark that students who have something are busy learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarship is both a funding award held by students and the erudition of scholars.

clue.text: Stalemate for rugby player

definitions.meaning: a deadlock where neither side gives way
the fly-half in rugby union is also called the ... half

explanation.surface: A deadlock involving a rugby player.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the stand-off (or fly-half) is the player who links the scrum-half with the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standoff, and the rugby position is called stand-off.

clue.text: Arm felt strange after end of each school break

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the single letter
the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from each
strange signals that the letters of arm and felt are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's arm feels odd after each school holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges ARMFELT into ALFTERM, placed 'after' H, the last letter of 'each'.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-term is the short holiday in the middle of a British school term.

clue.text: Stuff used as covering inside ship

definitions.meaning: material lining the inside of a coat or bin
a large passenger vessel such as an ocean-going one

explanation.surface: Material used to cover the interior of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A lining material is a liner, and a big passenger ship is an ocean liner.

clue.text: Gets better runs with friends

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
allies are friends and supporters

explanation.surface: A team recovers by scoring runs alongside its friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover strength, so someone who rallies improves after illness.

clue.text: Split in two say, and set off to gather crops

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken, giving a sound-alike rather than its spelling

parts.note: to halve something is to split it in two

indicators.note: off means the letters of set are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Divide it in two and set off to bring in the crops.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech 'halve' is said 'hahv', the same as HARV; 'off' then rearranges SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest is to reap and bring in the farm produce.

clue.text: Cut up rubbish fabric for suits

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word snip is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a snip is a cut
tripe means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone cuts up some poor fabric meant for making suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SNIP into PINS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is a cloth with thin vertical lines, classic for business suits.

clue.text: Mine's in the theatre

definitions.meaning: the orchestra area or the cheap seats at stalls level of a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone's mine is located in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a coal mine, and also the orchestra area of a theatre.

clue.text: Small French domesticated animal has it easy initially

parts.note: a pet is a domesticated animal

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of easy is used

explanation.surface: A small French pet has an easy life to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is borrowed from French, where it is the feminine form of 'small'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite is the French feminine word for little, used in English for a slight woman.

clue.text: The golden year concept

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: The idea of a golden year.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea or hypothesis.

clue.text: Everybody at home wrestling?

parts.note: all means everybody
in means at home

explanation.surface: Everybody is home, perhaps for a wrestling match.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: all-in wrestling is a freestyle form with few rules.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in describes freestyle wrestling, where almost any hold is allowed.

clue.text: It's gentler to change spectacles

definitions.note: plural noun, while the answer is a single pair of glasses

indicators.note: to change signals the letters of the previous words get rearranged

explanation.surface: It's gentler to change glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges GENTLERTO; the 'to' does double duty in the surface only, with its letters fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of glasses held up on a handle.

clue.text: Decide to stop excavation

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
a mine is an excavation

explanation.surface: Someone decides to halt a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or resolve a matter.

clue.text: Take time out perhaps using royal coach

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word out might be arranged another way

parts.note: R is short for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A royal coach is used to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal coach' suggests TUDOR, but the real parse is T + UTO (OUT rearranged, signalled by 'perhaps') + R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher, one who coaches a pupil.

clue.text: Tweezers for mushrooms

parts.note: ceps are a type of edible mushroom, the porcini

explanation.surface: Tweezers used for picking mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are pincers or tongs, a surgeon's tweezers.

clue.text: Teaching aid one cut out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of aid one cut are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A teaching aid was cut out of the budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Education is schooling or instruction.

clue.text: Narrow metal container is hot inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter for hot goes within the container

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A narrow metal container is hot inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin means slender or narrow.

clue.text: Pilot with many years in cheap marine accommodation

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A pilot spends many years in the cheapest berth at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-fare class of passenger accommodation on a ship.

clue.text: Plants man in toilet

indicators.note: in signals one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the gents is a men's public toilet
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man stands among plants in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'gents' is everyday British slang for a men's public lavatory, and 'Plants' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are blue-flowered alpine plants.

clue.text: Restrain vicious dog before starting

parts.note: a cur is a snappish, aggressive mongrel

indicators.note: starting means the opening letter of before is taken

explanation.surface: Hold back the savage dog before it gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb is to check or hold in check.

clue.text: Annoyed exclamation bishop has to endure it

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
to last is to endure

explanation.surface: An irritated cry as a bishop has to put up with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast it is a mild curse of frustration.

clue.text: Plays performed here and there at resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning the letters of there at are sorted again

explanation.surface: Plays are performed here and there at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as 're-sort', rearranging THEREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the building where dramas are staged.

clue.text: Coach's single item of footwear

definitions.meaning: one sports shoe of a pair

explanation.surface: A coach's single shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a coach, and also a sports shoe.

clue.text: Good scope for a sacrificial move

parts.note: ambit means scope or extent

explanation.surface: Good room for manoeuvre before a sacrificial move.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a gambit is an opening offering a pawn for advantage.

clue.text: Used to dig in a suit

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone used to dig while wearing a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are digging tools and one of the four card suits.

clue.text: In Greece, a top grade

definitions.meaning: the Greek letter corresponding to our a
the highest mark, as in a first-class result

explanation.surface: In Greece, a top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter and the top mark in some marking schemes.

clue.text: Separated people take time obtaining accommodation

parts.note: apart means separated
men stands for people

explanation.surface: A separated couple take time over finding a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms to live in.

clue.text: Woman's garment is cut in, a different way

indicators.note: a different way means the letters of cut in are put in another order

explanation.surface: A woman's dress is cut in a new style.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose sleeveless garment, often worn by women.

clue.text: Rotten flavouring put on game

parts.note: bad means rotten
mint is a common flavouring

explanation.surface: Bad-tasting flavouring is put on before a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock.

clue.text: Many a large safari park has resident antelope

indicators.note: resident means living within, so the letters sit inside the words many a large

explanation.surface: Many a large safari park has resident antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resident' shows the answer living inside 'Many a large'; 'safari park' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: It's different in the poetic version

indicators.note: different signals the letters of It's are made into a new order

explanation.surface: Something different appears in the poetic form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges ITS; the apostrophe moves to the front in the poet's contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets write the contraction 'tis for it is, an archaic form.

clue.text: Teachers daft for splitting shells

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
crackers means daft or mad

explanation.surface: Teachers are daft about cracking shells.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcrackers are a hinged tool used for breaking open hard nut casings.
